stories.headline: Son Heung-Min: Thomas Müller spot-on about lack of pressure in MLS
stories.summary: LAFC forward Son Heung-Min has backed Thomas Müller's comments about the "careless" playing style in the MLS and the lack of pressure that players feel due to the absence of a promotion/relegation system.
stories.body:
LAFC forward Son Heung-Min has backed Thomas Müller's comments about the "careless" playing style in the MLS and the lack of pressure that players feel due to the absence of a promotion/relegation system.

Last week, Vancouver Whitecaps star Müller said it is difficult to compare the MLS to the Premier League or other European leagues because "there is no relegation. There is no big pressure."

Son, who moved to the MLS in 2025 after a lengthy spell at Tottenham Hotspur, said Müller was "spot on" when asked about the German's remarks by reporters.

"The MLS is getting big, big name players are coming to the MLS but sometimes you feel there's less pressure because there isn't relegation.

"I can't control that but I'm enjoying this league...But I think Thomas was spot on. I thoroughly agree. He had an amazing career in the Bundesliga and he feels he's right to say it," the South Korea star said.

"I was in the Premier League -- every week, it's the biggest pressure. If you're not performing, if you're not playing well, if your team starts struggling or is in the bottom half of the table then you're having a difficult time.

"I think it makes it more fun. I want the best for the MLS, so maybe they can look into it and do something."

Müller, the most decorated German player of all time, sparked a conversation around the MLS' system of no promotion or relegation with his comments.

"[In Europe with relegation] The players have maybe no contracts for next year when you go down, so the playing style changes," the former Bayern Munich man said at the time. "When you play a bottom of the league team in Europe they fight for their lives. And sometimes I have the feeling, because of the [MLS] system, the playing style is a little bit more, let's say, optimistic, or careless, defensively.

- Philadelphia's Cavan Sullivan wins MLS Young Player of the Year award

- How B.J. Callaghan's long, winding coaching journey led to Nashville success

- Reports: Dynamo's Herrera charged with DWI, club aware of 'incident'

"So a little bit, just a little bit more, the French would say, laissez faire," he said. "That's maybe good for seeing some nice offensive plays when the games are opening up. When I compare it I see sometimes really, really good individual actions in players.

"What I miss sometimes is maybe the consistency, the good and the bad, the gap is bigger.

"[In MLS] There is, oh yeah, we do a rebuild," he said. "Nobody is happy to lose but it's totally different when you fight for getting relegated. Maybe yeah, you lose budget for the next year, the whole club. You lose people working at the club when the budget changes. It's totally different for fans."

stories.headline: Fantasy adds, NBA bets to make for Monday: Pick up Brook Lopez, Quentin Grimes
stories.summary: Andre Snellings breaks down Monday's NBA slate, highlighting the fantasy streamers to add and bets to make.
stories.body:
This NBA week opens with 10 games on the docket and one anticipated season debut from an All Star. Brandon Ingram is expected to make his first appearance of the season for the LA Clippers in their road tilt against the Houston Rockets. Ingram has been out recovering from offseason surgery on a partially torn Achilles tendon, but has ramped up his activity and should be on the court tonight. It hasn't been announced what type of minutes restriction he might be on, but after such a lengthy layoff some sort of minutes regimen should be expected.

The Clippers and the Rockets comprise one of the six games tonight featuring spreads of at least 8.5 points, with five of those spreads in double figures. The larger spreads indicate that several games have anticipated blowout potential, and blowouts can be challenging for both fantasy production and player props.

As such, it could be worth looking more closely at the three games featuring spreads of only 3.5 points tonight. The Memphis Grizzlies at the Charlotte Hornets, the Portland Trail Blazers at the Philadelphia 76ers and the Phoenix Suns at the New Orleans Pelicans are all expected to be closer, competitive games tonight. The Trail Blazers at the 76ers is the only game tonight between two teams that are both over .500, while the Suns at the Pelicans is the only game with a spread under four and an over/under line set above 230 (232.5 total).

These, and many other storylines will be on display in tonight's action. As always, let's dig deeper into the matchups to identify some potential fantasy streamers and betting angles of interest.

Fantasy stream team

Available in at least 50% of ESPN leagues.

Jalen Smith, PF/C, Chicago Bulls (rostered in 49.1% of ESPN leagues)

Quentin Grimes, SG/SF, Los Angeles Lakers (44.7%)

Grimes is expected to get his fifth straight start tonight in place of Austin Reaves (heel). Grimes popped for a career-high 47 points last Wednesday, and overall in his past four games he has averaged 25.5 PPG, 6.0 RPG and 5.0 3PG. He has slotted in perfectly as the second offensive option for the Lakers next to Luka Doncic.

Cam Spencer, SG/PG, Memphis Grizzlies (37.5%)

Spencer moved back to a reserve role when Ty Jerome returned from a four-game absence, but he still played 30 minutes and notched more than 30 fantasy points for the fifth straight game. In fact, in his past three appearances off the bench, Spencer has averaged 12.9 PPG, 4.3 APG and 2.0 3PG in 24.7 MPG.

Brook Lopez, C, LA Clippers (38.6%)

Lopez enters this game on a torrid scoring stretch, having notched 20 or more points in six of his last eight games including the last three straight. He has been particularly hot from behind the arc, averaging 2.3 3PG on 41.9 3P% to go along with 18.5 PPG and 5.8 RPG during that eight-game stretch.

Dre's best bets
Ty Jerome OVER 22.5 points (-119)

Jerome has been a potent scorer all season when health has allowed. He has had two short injury absences due to back/hip issues, and in the game leading up to and coming out of each absence he has scored in the teens. But in his other eight games, Jerome has averaged more than 28 PPG. Tonight, he faces a Hornets squad that has been torched for at least 26 points and three 3-pointers by an opposing player in four straight games.

Philadelphia 76ers -3.5 points vs. Portland Trail Blazers (-108)

The 76ers have won five straight games by an average of 7.6 PPG to move into a tie for the best record in the NBA (14-3). Meanwhile, after starting the season 9-3, the Trail Blazers have lost three of their last four games to fall into seventh place out West. The Trail Blazers are also playing their sixth straight road game while the 76ers are playing their second straight at home, which could play in the 76ers' favor as well.

Dillon Brooks OVER 15.5 points (-114)

Brooks is a streaky scorer who is in the midst of a hot streak. He had a similar scoring spree earlier in the season when he averaged 18.8 PPG over six games between October 24 and November 5. In his last three games, he has notched 20.7 PPG while shooting 51.0% from the field. Tonight, he'll be facing a friendly Pelicans defense also plays at the sixth-fastest pace in the league.

stories.headline: 2026-27 MLB free agency, trade grades: Offseason analysis
stories.summary: We've got you covered with grades and analysis on every winter signing and big offseason trade.
stories.body:
Hot stove season has finally begun!

The 2026-27 MLB offseason is officially here, and we have you covered with grades and analysis for every major signing and trade as this winter -- which is expected to include a labor stoppage -- unfolds.

Whether it's a franchise-changing free agent signing or an unexpected blockbuster trade, we'll weigh in with what it all means for next season and beyond.

ESPN MLB experts Bradford Doolittle and David Schoenfield will evaluate each move as it happens, so follow along here, as this story will continue to be updated. Check back in for all the most recent analysis.

Related links: Tracker | Top 50 free agents

Mets get help at first base with Goldschmidt

The deal: One year, $8 million

Grade: B

As Paul Goldschmidt has aged out of his peak seasons that culminated with the 2022 National League MVP Award, he has continued to do one thing exceptionally well: mash left-handers. Over the past two seasons, he has hit .317/.402/.572 against lefties -- the fifth-highest OPS among all hitters (Aaron Judge, Shea Langeliers, Coby Mayo and Jackson Chourio are ahead of him, in case you're curious).

Against left-handers, he strikes out just 14.8% of the time, but he hasn't sacrificed power, hitting 18 home runs in 306 at-bats. Against right-handers, however, he has been useless, putting up backup infielder numbers: .235/.271/.337 with 10 home runs in 528 at-bats. The Yankees gave him nearly 200 plate appearances against righties in 2026 for some reason, but Goldschmidt should be strictly viewed as a platoon bat at first base or DH.

Certainly, the Mets needed help at first base and/or DH: They were 28th in OPS at first base and 20th at DH. Between the two positions combined, the Mets were 29th in OPS, 29th in RBIs, 29th in batting average and 29th in on-base percentage. Goldschmidt should help, even in his age-39 season, but he's only one-fourth of the equation.

The problem here is it's hard to carry that kind of player with modern roster-building, when the four bench players will have to include a catcher, infielder and outfielder. The Mets are already rostering Mark Vientos, Jorge Polanco and Jared Young, all of whom shouldn't play any position other than first base. Brett Baty is around as a multiposition backup and Bo Bichette can serve as the emergency backup to Francisco Lindor at shortstop, so maybe there is enough versatility here.

Perhaps the best option will be playing Baty more in the outfield with Juan Soto getting regular DH time, and Goldschmidt then platooning with Polanco or Young at first base. If Polanco can find his 2025 stroke, that could work, and Young was at least not terrible (and he has torn up Triple-A for years, so maybe he can be moderately productive). Goldschmidt fills a role, but the real keys to a better offense for the Mets will be a healthier Soto and Lindor plus a much better Bichette (not to mention Carson Benge and A.J. Ewing improving in their sophomore seasons). If all that happens, this could end up being a dynamic lineup. -- Schoenfield

Big Apple blockbuster! Mets, Skubal agree to record deal

The deal: Nine years, $450 million

Grade: B+

It's not often that a two-time Cy Young winner still in his prime and regarded as one of the best starting pitchers in the game becomes available in free agency. These are potential franchise-altering difference-makers, maybe a final piece needed to build a World Series champion. If you have an owner who wants to win and is willing to spend the money, you make it happen at any cost.

Read the full grade here.

Yankees reinforce bullpen with Bednar, Loaisiga

The deals: David Bednar accepts one-year, $23.15 million qualifying offer; Jonathan Loáisiga agrees to two-year, $18 million deal

Grade: C+

Let's combine these two moves into one overall grade as the Yankees piece together the back end of their bullpen -- a pen that ranked second in the majors with a 3.13 ERA in 2026. The Yankees shoved Bednar into a corner by giving him a qualifying offer, which promised to limit his demand in free agency since he would have been tied to draft pick compensation. By accepting it, Bednar's salary is now the highest average salary for a reliever, topping Edwin Diaz's $23 million with the Dodgers.

Other than a blip in 2024, Bednar has been steady since 2021, first with the Pirates and then with the Yankees after coming over at the trade deadline in 2025, posting sub-3.00 ERAs in five of his six seasons, including 2.47 ERA in 2026 when he racked up 35 saves in 39 opportunities. He throws a four-seamer, splitter and curveball, with his splitter his big out pitch, holding batters to a .149 average in 2026 and .175 in 2025, with just one home run over the two seasons. His four-seamer can be more hittable, although he kept it in the park this past season. The Yankees love his toughness and showed their high regard for him in giving him the qualifying offer. He's not an A-plus closer, but he's very good and a safe bet on a one-year -- albeit expensive -- deal.

Loáisiga, meanwhile, returns to the club where he pitched from 2018 to 2025 -- although "pitched" is a loose description since he was often injured. In his one year with Arizona, he posted a 2.42 ERA across 67 innings, just the second time he's surpassed 50 innings. He still has an electric 98 mph sinker, although he fanned just 48 batters. Even for a sinker-reliant pitcher, that's a low total, although he did produce a high ground ball rate and a lot of soft contact. We'll see how that works without Geraldo Perdomo and Nolan Arenado behind him.

The problem is the durability history, and Loáisiga is replacing free agent Paul Blackburn, who had an amazing year, with a 1.59 ERA in 85 innings. Loáisiga isn't going to match that ERA or throw that many innings -- but Blackburn was unlikely to do that again, either. Overall, the Yankees have at least locked in their closer and top right-handed setup guy, although they are paying a steep price at $32 million to do it. -- Schoenfield

Rockies add pair of starters in deal with White Sox

Colorado Rockies get:

RHP Davis Martin

RHP Luis Castillo

Chicago White Sox get:

LHP Sean Sullivan

C Douglas Veliz

White Sox grade: C+

The White Sox appear to be spending proverbial money to spend proverbial money. That is to say, they are moving past the Castillo mistake from the last trade deadline -- one whose ramifications were primarily monetary -- and to do it, they are folding in a legitimate starter in Martin -- a pitcher who, for the first few weeks of the 2026 season, looked like a Cy Young candidate. They aren't spending actual money but are rearranging resources in hopes of spending money in a more productive way.

That's just reality, not an attempt to overhype Martin, whose season came unraveled the deeper we got into the calendar and who was ultimately not in position to help Chicago's staff once it reached the postseason. Still, he put up more than 140 innings in each of the past two seasons with a 104 ERA+ during the pre-arbitration phase of his service time window. He was a valuable player for Chicago and therefore is now that for Colorado.

This perspective speaks to how badly the White Sox wanted to clear Castillo off their books, and his departure -- which rids them of a $22.75 million 2027 salary plus a semi-unlikely vesting option for 2028 -- opens up the payroll so that Chicago can further upgrade a rotation it thinks it upgraded with the signing of Dustin May earlier this week.

Castillo was ghastly -- harsh as that sounds -- last season for the Mariners before Chicago acquired him at the trade deadline, and he was even worse after the deal. It was the first truly bad season of his mostly very good 10-year big league career, but it felt like it was one that was a result of trends that were years in the making. The one and truly virtuous aspect of this deal for the White Sox is that it rids them of the considerable risk that Castillo bounces back and justifies his sizable salary.

Sullivan is a long, lean lefty with so-so stuff who relies on deception -- perhaps not the soft-tossing lefty of yore, but someone along those lines. Veliz is a 17-year-old catcher who originally was signed for $50,000 out of Venezuela. Maybe someday you'll read his name again.

Chicago's grade is entirely provisional. The White Sox have opened up payroll space that needs to be parlayed into a meaningful upgrade. The 2027 rotation, once it's in place, will have some kind of configuration that includes May, an unsigned pitcher to be named and the other returnees to the staff. The gamble is that this new group will be better than simply running it back with Castillo while hoping for more consistency from Martin.

Right now, it's hard to say which path would have been better.

Rockies grade: B

I mean, why not? It's easy to make the crude argument against Castillo -- over 126 games for the Mariners, he went 43-40 with a 3.69 ERA while pitching half the time in one of baseball's most pitcher-friendly contexts. (During those seasons, his ERA was 3.07 at T-Mobile Park and 4.38 on the road.) Now he's headed to the wood-chipper of a pitching context at Coors Field and doing so at the nadir of his career.

Still, for the Rockies, it's a worthy gamble especially since it lands them Martin in the process. Is Martin the right pitcher for Coors Field? Who knows? But the still-new brain trust in Colorado needs to show it has real ideas about who will and who will not be able to function from the pitcher's mound in the Rockies' home venue.

Martin has real remaining upside, but Castillo is really the intriguing part here because he's a veteran with a lot to prove given the lack of long-term certainty around his contract status. Maybe he's done. Fine. It's only money, right? And you've still got Martin. But if Castillo flourishes by whatever definition that means when pitching in Coors, it's more than a productive performance for a team likely to land once again in the NL West cellar. It's a proof of concept. The Rockies need all of those they can get. -- Doolittle

Twins bring Gray back to Minnesota
The deal: Two years, $55 million

Grade: B+

Sonny Gray had one of the best seasons of his career with the Minnesota Twins back in 2023, when he made 32 starts, posted a 2.79 ERA and a 5.6 WAR, and finished second in the Cy Young Award voting. (He won just eight games, plagued by a lack of run support and a poor bullpen.) The Twins are hoping for a happy reunion, signing Gray to the largest total value free agent pitcher contract in franchise history (tied with a four-year deal for Ervin Santana back in 2015). The second year is a player option, so this could end up being a one-year deal.

This wasn't necessarily where everyone expected Gray to land, especially coming off a strong season with the Boston Red Sox. He finished 18-5, tied with Cristopher Sanchez for the major league lead in wins, while posting a 2.72 ERA, good for eighth in the majors. While Gray had some injuries earlier in his career, he has been durable across the past four seasons, averaging 30 starts and 175 innings. That almost makes him Old Hoss Radbourn in today's game. While Gray's ERA has jumped all over the place, his FIP (fielding independent pitching) speaks to more consistency, with marks of 3.40, 2.83, 3.12, 3.39 and 3.47 going back to 2022.

The negatives: Gray is 37 years old and his strikeout rate took a big dip in 2026, dropping from 28.4% over the previous two seasons to 21.8%. That's still playable -- the MLB average for starting pitchers was 21.9% -- but it's something to watch. However, he's such a smart pitcher -- mixing in six different pitches with excellent command -- that he can succeed even with a lower K rate.

It's a nice move for the Twins, who ranked 22nd in rotation ERA this past season. They've indicated an intent to keep Joe Ryan. Plus, Pablo Lopez is aiming to be ready by Opening Day in his return from Tommy John surgery, so Minnesota could roll out a rotation of Gray, Ryan, Lopez, Taj Bradley (their top starter in 2026 with 4.4 WAR) and Bailey Ober, with Dean Kremer, Connor Prielipp and Zebby Matthews as depth. Ryan, Lopez, Ober and Kremer are all in the final years of their deals, so there are trade possibilities here, especially since Minnesota needs to improve the bullpen.

Gray's contract projection was for two years and $42 million, so the deal comes in higher than that; this might be par for the course for starting pitchers given Dustin May's inflated three-year, $52.5 million deal with the Chicago White Sox. In one sense, the best-case scenario for the Twins is if Gray has another good season and he opts out. If he does have a good season and Lopez bounces back, this has a chance to be a really nice rotation, with Prielipp having breakout potential in his second year. And a good rotation in the American League Central will make the Twins contenders. -- Schoenfield

Mariners add Garcia to infield in six-player swap

Seattle Mariners get:

IF Maikel Garcia

RHP James McArthur

RHP L.P. Langevin

Kansas City Royals get:

RHP Bryce Miller

RHP Logan Evans

LHP Jose Ferrer

Mariners grade: A-

Garcia is the best player in the deal, and the difference is enough to make this a slam dunk win for Seattle. Nagging injuries undermined Garcia's 2026 season after his breakout the year before; but even so, his contract and patience at the plate remained well above average, and he was still one of baseball's top defensive third basemen. While the injuries cost him in the power department and on the bases, Garcia is entering his age-27 season as a good bet to bounce back to All-Star form. His well-documented penchant for self-improvement also supports the argument for positive regression.

Under contract through 2031 on team-friendly terms, Garcia is a major upgrade at a soft spot on the Mariners' depth chart. Seattle's defensive projection at the hot corner leaped from 21st to first in my system, and the offensive leap in runs from that spot was about 10 spots, to No. 12. Garcia's range will only help the overall infield defense, as he will team with Colt Emerson, Cole Young and Josh Naylor to give Seattle a pretty dynamic group.

The Mariners had the kind of surplus on their organizational rotation chart to easily absorb the loss of Miller. Similar to last year, they look a little thin in bullpen lefties, but Ferrer didn't prove to be the splash addition in that role Seattle hoped for anyway. McArthur is a sneaky get here. He hasn't pitched in the majors since 2024 because of injury but was closing games for the Royals before getting hurt. He's a worthy flier. Langevin is a lower-level prospect, a righty with big strikeout rates and shaky command.

The Mariners' right-now win projection climbs over 90 with this trade, and at 67% division title odds, Seattle is a heavy early favorite in a soft division. This trade only bolsters the chances that the Mariners bounce back in 2027 to become the team we thought they were in 2026.

Royals grade: C-

The Royals just don't have the kind of organizational depth to be trading one of their few difference-makers for a package of pitchers who in total upgrade their staff only marginally and offer little collective upside. In the near term, the trade makes the Royals worse, and the problems only compound from here given that they had Garcia under team control for so long.

Miller moves right into a middle-of-the-rotation slot for the Royals, and if Michael Wacha declines, it's possible Miller will be Kansas City's top starter next season. Still, Miller, 27, has a career ERA+ of 95 and is at 80 over the past two seasons, both of which have been undermined by injury. For the Royals, the hope would be that Miller is ready to take the kind of leap that Wacha and Seth Lugo did when they joined the Royals. And to be fair, Miller's Statcast metrics definitely suggest that could happen.

Ferrer, as mentioned, had a poor season in Seattle after being acquired for catcher Harry Ford. Ferrer has a career OPS+ of 96 but still becomes the Royals' top bullpen lefty, almost by default. Evans was a ranked organizational prospect in Seattle and had a decent debut season in 2025. He underwent Tommy John surgery, the internal brace version, in January. He projected with mid- to lower-rotation upside before getting hurt.

The instant change in the Royals' projection kind of tells the story. The new pitchers are pushing not-great pitchers down the depth chart, so Kansas City's profile improves by about 16 runs on the prevention side. Garcia's defensive loss is fairly marginal for Kansas City, as Nick Loftin is a good defender, as well. But the loss of the bat is about a 17-run hit for the Royals' run production.

The end result? The same amount of bad, just shaped differently. The Royals should have received more for a player of Garcia's ability and contract. -- Doolittle

White Sox add midrotation piece with May
The deal: Three years, $52.5 million

Grade: D+

We've had two significant signings off the free agent market so far, and both involve freshly minted ex-Milwaukee Brewers: After Jake Bauers landed with the Boston Red Sox on Friday, the Chicago White Sox plucked Dustin May off the championship Milwaukee pitching staff.

Whereas Boston was banking on Bauers' 2026 breakout being his current true talent level, the White Sox are perhaps taking a bigger gamble that May's past five years do not represent his real level of ability. Since his early shine as a top Los Angeles Dodgers prospect, which included some promising early work in the majors, May's career has been journeyman-like. Around injuries that cost him the 2024 season, he has put up 0.9 bWAR with a 91 ERA+ over 356 big-league innings for the period covering 2022 through last season.

May became a fallback addition for the Brewers at the 2026 trade deadline after more glitzy pursuits (ahem, Tarik Skubal) fell short. May put up a 106 ERA+ for the St. Louis Cardinals before the trade and, given the Brewers' track record with acquired pitchers, you had to figure the move boded well for an even better post-trade performance. But that's not what happened. May had a 5.65 ERA and 75 ERA+ over 10 starts for the Brewers and was not a core part of Milwaukee's postseason rotation.

This uninspiring platform performance partially explains the grade above, but only partially. We'll see how things shake out in the market when we have more signings to work from -- May is the first pitcher to land a sizable deal -- but this seems like an overpay at least in terms of years. ESPN's Kiley McDaniel projected a one-year, $14 million deal for May, while a consensus projection from various outlets looked something more like two years, $24.7 million.

The White Sox are likely banking on May's tantalizing tracking data, which in 2026 had him in the 85th percentile in fastball velocity (average of 96.8 mph) and 72nd percentile in extension. Indeed, my own projection model sees enough in May keeping his value that it suggested a three-year, $45.9 million deal would be justified, which at least is in the neighborhood of what he got from the White Sox.

As it stands, May slots in behind Grant Taylor in the revamped Chicago rotation, just ahead of Sean Burke and Luis Castillo. Ah, Castillo: Is he a cautionary tale for a White Sox approach that liked him, as it likes May, despite underwhelming results before the deal? We'll see. May is also pushing pitchers such as David Sandlin and Davis Martin down in the pecking order, though there's no guarantee he's going to be that much better than them, if at all. I've got May adding 0.9 wins to Chicago's right-now roster, which pushes its 2027 playoff odds up by about three percentage points.

That's fairly marginal when you remember that the White Sox were overachievers in 2026. It was a great story, but it also means their starting baseline is somewhere south of the 84 games they won in 2026. If they are really looking to bolster their chances heading into 2027 -- and beyond -- then opportunity cost comes into play even though the White Sox should have some remaining spending capacity, or at least you would hope so. Would a little patience have netted them someone like Sonny Gray, Michael King or Freddy Peralta?

If the White Sox still go after someone like that and the May signing doesn't end up as their one big rotation splash, then maybe we push that grade up to the C-minus range. Given what we know at the moment, though, I'm underwhelmed. -- Doolittle

Red Sox get offensive boost with Bauers addition
The deal: Four years, $58 million

Grade: A

The Red Sox weren't high on anybody's list of teams likely to sign Jake Bauers given they already have an All-Star first baseman in Willson Contreras, but this signing is an early candidate for best move of the offseason. The grade reflects two thoughts: (1) that Bauers' breakout -- he finished 11th in the majors in OPS and third in on-base percentage this past season -- is for real; and (2) that the contract is a steal at $14.5 million per year.

Bauers will be entering his age-31 season, and, of course, spent years struggling in the majors before finally figuring things out, so while there would generally be concern that his 2026 season was a fluke, all the advanced metrics suggest the opposite. His Statcast numbers: 93rd percentile bat speed, 94th percentile hard-hit rate, 93rd percentile chase rate, 98th percentile walk rate. Those are real skills that aren't going to diminish overnight and should allow him to remain a productive hitter (he even hit left-handers well, so should project as a full-time player). Everyone saw the quality of his at-bats during the postseason throughout the Milwaukee Brewers' title run; he was named MVP of the National League Championship Series.

As for the contract, compare it to Josh Naylor's deal last year, when he signed a five-year, $92.5 million contract with the Seattle Mariners. Naylor was two years younger, but he was coming off a 129-OPS+, 3.0-WAR season compared with Bauers' 140 OPS+ and 3.3 WAR. Yes, Naylor had the longer track record of success but less power and a lower OBP. Signing Bauers for $58 million looks like a potential bargain.

Contreras is under contract for 2027 with a team option for 2028 and is the better fielder, so Bauers slots in as the DH. That leaves Roman Anthony, Ceddanne Rafaela and Wilyer Abreu in the outfield. Masataka Yoshida is still around for one more year as a backup, and the Red Sox will likely look to trade Jarren Duran, who still has two years of team control but is estimated to make $11.1 million in arbitration. With Duran coming off a bad season at the plate, the Red Sox might non-tender him if they can't trade him.

No doubt there will be criticism that the Red Sox needed a right-handed batter instead, but they actually had a slightly higher OPS against left-handers (.734 to .710). They just needed a good hitter, regardless of which side of the plate he stands on.

Remember that they also acquired the right-handed Curtis Mead from the Washington Nationals only to see him get injured in his first game with them. He'll be back and should slot in at second base. Boston also has shortstop Franklin Arias, one of the top three or four prospects in the minors who demolished Double- and Triple-A this year. Indeed, if Bauers comes close to his 2026 numbers and Anthony hits like everyone thought he was going to in 2026, this could be one of the best lineups in the league:

LF Anthony (L)

RF Abreu (L)

1B Contreras (R)

DH Bauers (L)

CF Rafaela (R)

2B Mead (R)

C Adley Rutschman (S)

SS Arias (R) / Trevor Story (R)

3B Caleb Durbin (R)

As for the Brewers, it's sad to see a postseason hero go, although not necessarily unexpected. They could have afforded this contract, but they have first-base prospects just about ready in Andrew Fischer, who led the minors with 48 home runs, and Blake Burke, who hit 34 home runs and stole 29 bases. They also have Andrew Vaughn on hand as a placeholder if Fischer and Burke aren't ready. Plus, they might need this money to sign William Contreras to a long-term extension. The Brewers will be fine. -- Schoenfield

Braves bolster bullpen by landing Phillips
The deal: Three years, $35 million

Grade: B-

The Atlanta Braves don't go after the biggest free agents -- B.J. Upton's $75 million deal in 2013 remains the largest free agent contract in franchise history -- but president of baseball operations Alex Anthopoulos does like to strike as early as possible in the offseason, and he did that again with Evan Phillips.

Phillips will essentially take the roster spot of Raisel Iglesias, so the Braves will get a little younger and maybe a little better, although Iglesias had a good season as the closer in 2026 following some bumps in 2025. The Braves had one of the best bullpens in the majors this past year, leading in win probability added while ranking fourth in ERA and sixth in OPS allowed. Iglesias departs as a free agent, but Didier Fuentes or Robert Suarez can replace him as the ninth-inning guy, with Phillips likely slotting in as a setup man alongside lefties Dylan Lee and Dylan Dodd.

Phillips was one of the best relievers in the majors with the Dodgers in 2022-23 before suffering shoulder and elbow injuries at the end of the 2024 season and finally undergoing Tommy John surgery in June 2025. He returned to make 31 appearances with the Dodgers in 2026, finishing with 33 strikeouts and just six walks in 26 innings. The stuff looked good -- he was throwing a little harder than pre-injury -- although he did serve up five home runs, and his injury history makes a three-year deal a little risky.

The belief was that the Braves' pitching priority this offseason would be a starter, but signing Phillips will allow them to stretch out Fuentes as a starter in spring training. He does have a three-pitch arsenal in his fastball, slider and splitter, and he has thrown a curveball in the past, so as effective as Fuentes was in relief as a rookie in 2026, it makes sense to see if it can work out for him in the rotation. -- Schoenfield

Tigers kick off free agency with Pagan deal
The deal: One year, $11.5 million

Grade: C

A key reason the Detroit Tigers finished 76-86 despite a plus-71 run differential was the bullpen: Despite finishing 12th in ERA, it ranked 26th in win probability added, so it performed worse in high-leverage situations. Out with Kenley Jansen, in with Emilio Pagan, who has been the Reds' closer the past two seasons.

Jansen was only 22-for-28 in saves in 2026, so maybe Pagan is only a small upgrade, but like Jansen, Pagan has been prone to the home run, serving up 17 in 111⅓ innings over the past two seasons. The Tigers are betting that getting out of Cincinnati -- where he allowed 12 of those 17 home runs -- will help. Pagan is a three-pitch reliever, with a splitter that he throws primarily to left-handers and a cutter he throws to right-handers. But his 95 mph fastball is rather pedestrian for a modern closer, and batters have hit 12 home runs off it the past two seasons.

Pagan is also turning 36 years old and his fastball velo dropped from 95.8 mph in 2025 to 94.9 in 2026, so there are a couple of red flags here. The Tigers had to add somebody to the bullpen, and doing so before the anticipated lockout is logical, but Pagan projects as a midtier closer rather than the elite guy Detroit needs. Kyle Finnegan and Will Vest both struggled in 2026, so the Tigers could still nab a reliable right-handed setup guy. -- Schoenfield

stories.headline: Champions League Power Rankings before MD5: Who's No. 1?
stories.summary: The UEFA Champions League is going at full speed, and we're beyond the halfway point of the league phase. Injuries are starting to pile up. Where does your club rank?
stories.body:
We're officially past the midway point of the UEFA Champions League league phase as the 2026-27 European season rumbles on, and the grind of the calendar is beginning to take its toll on the elite teams, with injuries starting to pile up. Harry Kane (Bayern Munich), Désiré Doué (Paris Saint-Germain) and David Raya (Arsenal) were all sidelined this weekend with issues of varying severity, and it's only going to get more grueling as we head toward the hectic festive period and, beyond that, the January transfer window.

So what has it done to the standings? Throughout the competition, we will be asking our writers, editors and other experts to rank the top 10 teams in the tournament in terms of who they think are the strongest and most likely to win it all. Here are your Champions League Power Rankings going into a fun week.

UCL Power Rankings before Matchday 5

1. PARIS SAINT-GERMAIN

- Previous rank: 1

- Games since MD3: defeated Lyon 2-0; defeated Le Havre 5-1; defeated Villarreal 6-0; defeated Troyes 1-0; defeated Nice 3-2

- MD5 opponent: vs. AS Roma (Wednesday)

Would anyone bet against them winning it all a third straight time? Our voters were nearly unanimous -- 15 of 17 -- in crowning the French champions and back-to-back Champions League winners as the best team in this competition, but there are tough tests to come.

PSG continue to look sharp and ruthless domestically, which isn't normally their rhythm at this time of year. (Folks will remember that they generally wake up, form-wise, after Christmas, at least in recent seasons.) Ferran Torres keeps showing why he was such a savvy summer signing from Barcelona, chipping in eight goals and an assist as an occasional starter, with the likes of Senny Mayulu -- one of 12 players to get on the score sheet in Ligue 1 this season -- also stepping up to contribute in the attacking third.

They were managing without Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, who tore his ACL in October and faces a lengthy spell on the sideline, but Saturday's season-ending knee injury suffered by Doué in this weekend's win over Nice will tax their reserves over the course of a grueling campaign. Up next is a potentially tricky midweek date with Roma who, despite losing to Man United in Matchday 4, have one of the stingiest defenses in Serie A (11 goals conceded in 12 games).

2. BARCELONA

- Previous rank: 2

- Games since MD3: lost 2-1 vs. Real Madrid; defeated Alaves 6-1; defeated Aston Villa 3-0; defeated Atletico Madrid 2-1; defeated Villarreal 3-2

- MD5 opponent: at Sabah FK (Wednesday)

The Spanish champions continue to be box-office entertainment every week. They simply do not believe in drawing games; every single one of their games this season has ended with a decisive winner and loser, with their back-to-back losses to PSG and Real Madrid surrounded by wins up and down the schedule. Since the Clasico setback it has largely been business as usual, with big wins over Alaves and Villa followed by a very different pair of comeback victories at Atletico and home to Villarreal. Sunday's win had the feel of a predator toying with its prospective dinner, as Villarreal scored twice in the opening seven minutes to daze Lamine Yamal & Co. early, only for the champs to respond with three goals in 10 second-half minutes and a three-point lead at the top of LaLiga.

Like PSG, they have a simmering injury concern to their defensive corps, with several front-line defenders in various stages of rehab or treatment: Andreas Christensen has managed just 30 minutes of game time since mid-September, Pau Cubarsí's health is being monitored after a hip injury on international duty, and Jules Koundé/Eric García are just coming back from absences of their own. Rodri's ongoing fitness is a worry too as the best choice to shield a vulnerable back line, but as long as they are scoring goals by the bucketload -- their 51 in 13 LaLiga games is more than the bottom four teams in the table combined -- it feels like a minor concern. That said, Hansi Flick's side will need to tighten up once we get into the business end of this competition.

3. ARSENAL

- Previous rank: 3

- Games since MD3: defeated Everton 2-0; lost 5-3 on penalties vs. Fleetwood Town (Carabao Cup); defeated Liverpool 1-0; defeated Slavia Prague 2-1; defeated Hull 1-0; drew 2-2 vs. Newcastle

- MD5 opponent: vs. Borussia Dortmund (Tuesday)

The Gunners already have a six-point lead atop the Premier League after just 11 games, which feels like business as usual for Mikel Arteta's side, but the manner in which they slumped to a draw at Newcastle on Saturday shows that this side isn't quite at the juggernaut levels it achieved last season. Their aggressive press yielded the opening goal, when Kai Havertz snagged the ball from Lewis Hall and teed up Eberechi Eze, but Noni Madueke whiffed before halftime to double their lead and Arsenal crumbled after the break, conceding twice. Noni Madueke eventually atoned by rifling in the equalizer, but the loss of control and absence of ruthlessness will have Arsenal's rivals on notice.

This week's visit of Dortmund has all the hallmarks of a trap game, considering BVB are having a superb season so far and Arteta will have one eye on next weekend's visit of Man City to the Emirates instead. Shrugging off Saturday's torpor and asserting dominance over Niko Kovac & Co. on Tuesday will be essential to demoralizing the chasing pack.

4. REAL MADRID

- Previous rank: 6

- Games since MD3: defeated Barcelona 2-1; defeated Racing Santander 3-0; defeated AEK Athens 3-2; defeated Valencia 3-0; defeated Celta Vigo 2-1

- MD5 opponent: vs. PSV Eindhoven (Tuesday)

Since Jose Mourinho announced his return to the Bernabeu this summer, we've been wondering when things would start to come apart at the seams. All the ingredients were present: a grouchy manager with a chip on his shoulder and no filter, a star-studded but temperamental squad in need of careful coaching, a demanding fanbase that's impatient for success after a couple of seasons without silverware. And yet, everything looks kinda good at the moment? They won the Clasico, are unbeaten since Sept. 20's Madrid derby, and Mourinho is managing his way out of sticky situations with smart substitutions, canny motivation and a sense of calm we've not really seen from him to date.

However, you can see cracks here and there -- it took some inspired second-half subs to overcome Celta Vigo, who scored first -- and Mourinho will need to be gentle in how he keeps his attacking corps happy. Vinicius Jr. is back from suspension (and a nice international break with Brazil), and will be keen for playing time regardless of how well Yan Diomande, Arda Güler, Carlos Espí and Jude Bellingham have looked in support of Kylian Mbappé.

Mourinho's magic and the relative stability/fitness have vaulted them into the top four of our rankings for the first time this season; will it stick?

5. BAYERN MUNICH

- Previous rank: 4

- Games since MD3: defeated Freiburg 3-1; defeated Magdeburg 6-1; drew 2-2 vs. Borussia Dortmund; defeated Atletico Madrid 2-0; defeated Mainz 2-1; drew 1-1 vs. Koln

- MD5 opponent: at Lille (Wednesday)

Bayern continue to chug along domestically -- wobble in Der Klassiker aside -- but the injuries to Kane and Michael Olise in Friday's draw with Koln will hurt their chances of keeping up with their rivals in the Champions League. Kane won't be back for months after ankle surgery, while Olise (bruised foot) joins the likes of Luis Díaz, Ismael Saibari and Serge Gnabry in the ranks of hobbled playmakers, all of which will test manager Vincent Kompany's abilities over the coming weeks.

The traditional Bundesliga "winterpause" means it won't hurt them much domestically, but our voters have downgraded them in the context of the Champions League until they figure out some viable alternatives.

6. MANCHESTER CITY

- Previous rank: 5

- Games since MD3: lost 2-1 vs. Aston Villa; defeated Brighton 4-3 on penalties (Carabao Cup); lost 1-0 vs. Brighton; defeated RB Leipzig 3-2; lost 3-1 vs. Nottingham Forest; drew 1-1 vs. Fulham

- MD5 opponent: vs. Napoli (Tuesday)

Things have not been going well for Enzo Maresca & Co. in recent weeks, with dropped points in the Premier League and a slew of bereft, listless performances regardless of results. Are we finally seeing the toll of the Premier League's charges -- with the appeals and punishments processes happening on parallel timelines since the news broke at the end of September -- on this squad and these players? There's a fog around the Etihad, one in which their identity, effectiveness and performance are struggling to be seen.

The midfield has been a mess since Rodri left for Barcelona, with Elliot Anderson (who scored a superb goal in the draw vs. Fulham) and Ayyoub Bouaddi (only 19) still figuring out how to mesh with Enzo Fernández and the passel of high-class attackers further ahead. The defense is also creaking in the worst ways, with Rúben Dias looking vulnerable and only the occasional heroics from Gianluigi Donnarumma keeping them in games.

There's no need to panic yet, but the fans are restless, the uncertainty around their potential punishments is overwhelming, and the vibes are sour. However, our voters still see them as a credible contender in Europe given the raw talent up and down the roster; if they can harness some momentum and secure a top-eight finish (and first-round playoff bye) in the Champions League, they can still make a deep, impactful run.

7. LIVERPOOL

- Previous rank: 7

- Games since MD3: defeated Brighton 2-0; defeated Chelsea 6-5 on penalties (Carabao Cup); lost 1-0 vs. Arsenal; lost 3-2 vs. Fenerbahce; defeated Crystal Palace 3-1; defeated Manchester United 4-0

- MD5 opponent: at Club Brugge (Wednesday)

Liverpool have looked better and more effective in the Champions League this season -- Fenerbahce defeat aside -- given that their playmakers generally have more time and space on the ball in Europe, but the Reds are turning the corner domestically as well. After months of two-steps-forward-one-step-back form and results, Andoni Iraola's vision is starting to take shape.

It's been far from linear progress, of course -- Bradley Barcola, Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak have all scored in recent games despite also looking completely peripheral in others -- and the optimal midfield combination has yet to be figured out, but the defensive platform provided by Alisson, Virgil van Dijk and Jérémy Jacquet has brought a welcome stability to a team that leaked goals all of last season. Ronald Araujo has won hearts and minds at Anfield, too, with the all-gas, no-brakes manner in which he insists on covering every inch of grass, and Rio Ngumoha continues to dazzle with skills and impact far beyond his years.

A tough run of league fixtures will take them into the always hectic festive period, but they will need to show the same ruthlessness against Club Brugge in midweek that they showed against Man United on Sunday.

8. COMO

- Previous rank: N/R

- Games since MD3: defeated Sassuolo 2-0; defeated Torino 3-1; defeated Venezia 1-0; defeated Lens 9-1; lost 2-0 vs. Inter Milan; defeated Cagliari 2-0

- MD5 opponent: vs. AEK Athens (Tuesday)

It seems crazy that only now, as we approach the end of November, are Como making it into our Power Rankings. It's not for me to say if our collective disrespect is serving as motivational material for Cesc Fabregas & Co. or not, but the Italian upstarts are fully deserving of a spot among the tournament favorites. If the nine-goal game against Lens didn't do it for you, what about them having an 8-2-2 record in Serie A with a squad averaging under 26 years old per player?

Fabregas is shaping up to be the next big thing in coaching based on how he's taking this tiny tourist town team from the sporting doldrums and into the spotlight, with Nico Paz the straw stirring the drink in attacking midfield to make it all click. He's got a ton of help, too -- Anastasios Douvikas is no household name but has 11 goals in 16 games, while Martin Baturina and Maximo Perrone are clever contributors -- and their press-heavy, quick-passing style is overwhelming opponents in all competitions.

It's too early to admit them to European soccer's highest tier, but they can make waves in the Champions League with a favorable draw and a clean bill of health across their squad.

9. INTER MILAN

- Previous rank: 9

- Games since MD3: defeated Fiorentina 2-1; defeated Venezia 2-0; lost 3-1 vs. AC Milan; defeated Feyenoord 3-0; defeated Como 2-0; drew 4-4 vs. Atalanta

- MD5 opponent: vs. Stuttgart (Wednesday)

Inter Milan are an Italian institution and the defending Serie A champions, but they rank below Como heading into Matchday 5! Our voters aren't quite convinced that Cristian Chivu's side has what it takes to contend for the Champions League right now -- Inter were runners-up in 2024-25 as PSG claimed their first, only to fall in the knockout phase play-off round to Bodo/Glimt, which may be weighing heavy on our electorate. If that didn't do it, Sunday's stunning draw at struggling Atalanta, in which they let 3-1 and 4-2 leads slip away with a litany of individual errors -- will have soured them to whether this team has what it takes.

The bright spot right now is Pio Esposito, who has scored eight goals in his last five games for club and country, and with Lautaro Martínez coming back to full fitness, Inter has enough firepower to blow most opponents away. But Chivu needs his team to tighten up quick before they lose sight of the Serie A leaders (Inter are third after 12 games) and the points gap in the Champions League becomes too big to overcome down the stretch.

10. ATLÉTICO MADRID

- Previous rank: 8

- Games since MD3: defeated Deportivo Coruna 2-1; defeated Levante 2-0; lost 2-0 vs. Bayern Munich; lost 2-1 vs. Barcelona, defeated Getafe 3-0

- MD5 opponent: vs. Viking (Wednesday)

Diego Simeone's side is losing the games you'd expect it to (Bayern, Barca) and picking up points everywhere else, which feels par for the course for LaLiga's third-biggest team. Despite being 23rd of 36 teams at the UCL midway point, with just four points (and one win) to their name, Atleti's pedigree still resonates among our voters when it comes the Power Rankings.

Sunday's win over Getafe was a milestone for Simeone -- his 345th win makes him LaLiga's all-time winningest manager -- and showcased the electricity in his squad that still makes voters feel so fondly for the talent. Julián Álvarez hasn't scored for Atleti in over a month but notched two assists this weekend as the de facto center forward, Álex Baena has made the wing position his own, and U.S. midfielder Johnny Cardoso also found the net.

Dropped out: Aston Villa

Other teams receiving votes

Borussia Dortmund, AS Roma, Aston Villa, Sporting CP, Man United

VOTERS

Our global panel includes writers and editors around FC and our global soccer desks: Tony Mabert, Jon Molyneux-Carter, Alex Kirkland, Bill Connelly, Tom Hamilton, Armando Neria, Rob Dawson, Nicholas Som, Austin Lindberg, Gustavo Hofman, James Tyler, Gab Marcotti, Mariano Mancuso, James Olley, Sam Marsden and Beth Lindop.

stories.headline: NHL Tonight: A seven-game Thanksgiving week appetizer on Monday
stories.summary: Find game previews, betting intel, broadcast information, stats and highlights here.
stories.body:
This will be a special week for hockey fans. Thursdays are typically a heavy night on the calendar, but with American Thanksgiving taking place this week there will be no NHL hockey being played.

To make up for it, there will be 14 games on Wednesday, 15 on Friday and 13 on Saturday.

And of course, a reminder (or new intel for the new fans out there): Since 2005-06, around 77% of the teams in playoff position as of American Thanksgiving have maintained that spot at the season's end.

On Monday, it's an appetizer course, with seven games on the calendar.

Read on for a look at what you need to know for each game, including betting info and broadcast details.

Odds are provided by DraftKings and subject to change.

Columbus Blue Jackets at New Jersey Devils

7 p.m. ET (NHL Network) | NJ -205, O/U: 6.5

After allowing nine goals to the Blues on Saturday, this game is an opportunity for the Devils to get their goal-suppression capabilities back up to standard. The Blue Jackets have scored 2.48 goals per game this season, which is dead last in the NHL.

On the other end of the ice, the Devils will be led by their top line of Jack Hughes (29 points in 23 games), Jesper Bratt (22) and Arseny Gritsyuk (17).

And whether it's Connor Hellebuyck or Jake Allen starting in the Devils' crease, they'll be tasked with keeping Kent Johnson (22 points in 21 games) and Zach Werenski (20) & Co. away from the promised land.

Los Angeles Kings at Montreal Canadiens

7:30 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | MTL -148, O/U: 6.5

This is the final game in a four-game Eastern road trip for the Kings, and it's possible that Artemi Panarin may return for this one after missing rejoining the team Saturday following a personal absence.

For his career, Panarin has 35 points in 26 regular-season games against the Habs.

The big news is that recent trade addition Dylan Larkin will be making his debut for the Canadiens in this one.

Montreal followed up statement wins over the Devils and Hurricanes with a loss to the Flyers on Saturday and will be looking to start another winning streak here.

Cole Caufield remains the Habs' top goal scorer, with 12, but hasn't netted one since Nov. 12. Lane Hutson is the leading assist man for Montreal, with 19.

Calgary Flames at Ottawa Senators

7:30 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | OTT -218, O/U: 5.5

This is Calgary's first trip to the Eastern time zone this season, and it'll be a rude awakening squaring off against one of the teams fighting for the top spot in the Atlantic Division.

The Flames are 31st in scoring this season (2.50 goals per game) and it's tough to see that rate improving if the Sens start Linus Ullmark. The veteran Swede has gone 11-1-0 this season, with a 1.47 goals-against average and .937 save percentage; he's the league leader in both of those rate categories.

Calgary will be tasked with slowing down a Senators offense led by a leveled-up Tim Stutzle. The No. 3 pick from 2020 is on pace for 45 goals and 108 points, both of which would be career highs.

Toronto Maple Leafs at New York Islanders

7:30 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | NYI -148, O/U: 6.5

Time for another showdown between the most recent No. 1 picks, as Gavin McKenna and the Leafs make their only trip to Long Island of the season to take on Matthew Schaefer and the Isles.

The teams split their previous matchups -- both played in Toronto -- with the Leafs winning 2-1 on Sept. 30 while the Islanders won 4-1 on Oct. 17.

That's about all that's equal between the clubs at this point, as the Leafs' losing streak has run to nine games and they are last in the Atlantic, while the Islanders have points in their past seven games (four wins and three losses in OT/SO), putting them right in the wild-card mix.

And as for those top picks, Schaefer continues to improve somehow and is up to 26 points through 22 games. McKenna has 14 points through 25 games, as analysts (both professional and amateur) continue to question Toronto's coaching staff about his usage (or lack thereof).

Utah Mammoth at Winnipeg Jets

7:30 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | UTA -112, O/U: 6.5

This will be the first of four matchups this season between these Central Division foes, who are now much closer in the standings than some would have projected a month ago.

Through 24 games for each club, the Mammoth have 27 standings points and a minus-1 goal differential while the Jets have 26 and a minus-7. So who comes out on top in this one?

Both teams have shown they can score -- Utah's per-game rate is a bit higher (3.33) than Winnipeg's (3.08), but the Jets did just hang eight on the Stars on Nov. 12.

So it could come down to which team is more effective at preventing goals, which has been an issue at times for both.

Anaheim Ducks at Seattle Kraken

9:40 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | SEA -115, O/U: 6.5

stories.headline: Guimarães: Newcastle fans that booed me 'can't delete my history with the club'
stories.summary: Bruno Guimarães has told the Newcastle fans who booed his return to St James Park that they "cannot delete the history I have with the club."
stories.body:
Bruno Guimarães has told the Newcastle fans who booed his return to St James Park that they "cannot delete the history I have with the club."

Guimarães was loudly jeered before, during and after Arsenal's 2-2 draw last Saturday in his first appearance back since a £75 million ($97.7m) summer move to the Gunners.

The 29-year-old spent five seasons on Tyneside and became the first Newcastle captain to lift a trophy in 56 years after beating Liverpool in the 2025 Carabao Cup Final.

Guimarães was a hugely popular figure but the angry reaction from many supporters left the Brazilian in no uncertain terms about where he now stands.

Asked about the contrast between that reaction and the instant backing from Arsenal supporters, Guimarães said on Monday: "The welcome has been amazing, I think they have been so good for me. I want to thank them for their support.

"For the Newcastle fans, I cannot control the fans. They can do whatever they want. The only thing they cannot do is delete the history I have with the club. But I cannot control the fans and that's all."

Guimarães, who has made 15 appearances for the Gunners to date, also hailed the impact Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta is having on his game through a "crazy" attention to detail.

- Arsenal's near-collapse at Newcastle is a wake-up call

- David Raya to be assessed after leaving Arsenal's draw at Newcastle with injury

"Mikel is unbelievable," he added. "As a manager, he is so focused on the small details, the way you control the ball, the way that you cannot be aligned with your opposite side -- some details that I never heard before.

"I just found out listening to him here, very small details, he is so crazy a little bit with these small details and I try to take as much as I can because he is so passionate on the small details.

"He always says to the midfield to not be aligned with the opposition, to give you two or three seconds ahead of them. He showed some clips of me at Newcastle and some clips of me here where he thinks I could do different [things]. I like to keep it a bit more private but he is trying to take me to another level."

Every practice and qualifying session as well as the race itself will be available to watch on Sky Sports F1. The sessions are also on Sky Sports Main Event.

For non-subscribers, highlights of the Qatar Grand Prix will be on free-to-air television on Channel 4.

In the U.S., subscribers can watch every session on Apple TV, via a new F1 channel on the platform.

Lusail Circuit

The Qatar Grand Prix takes place under the floodlights at the Lusail Circuit. It is one of the most demanding on the calendar with long straights and sweeping high-speed corners coupled with intense heat and humidity, making conditions for the cars and drivers difficult.

It was originally built as a motorbike circuit before it joined the F1 calendar in 2021 on a 10-year contract. Qatar did not host a race in 2022 as they focused on the FIFA World Cup.

The weather for the Qatar Grand Prix is forecast to be sunny with a gentle breeze across the weekend. It's a night race so conditions are dry with highs of 24°C on Sunday.

McLaren's Piastri pipped teammate Norris to pole position as the battle for the world title continued with two races remaining.

During the race, Red Bull's Verstappen benefited from a McLaren strategy error to win his seventh race of the season, taking the three-way title race to the season finale in Abu Dhabi.

Piastri was leading the race and Norris was running in third, but the Papaya team decided against pitting under the Safety Car. Piastri ended the race in second, with Norris in fourth.

Who will win this year?

Verstappen looked unstoppable in Las Vegas and will be targeting his fifth win of the season in Qatar.

Mercedes' Russell was well in the mix last time out but will be looking to respond after Verstappen said the Englishman was "so far below his level" as their feud intensified.

Both teams look strong, so the rivalry could well continue in Qatar. Drivers up and down the grid will also be limited to 27 laps on each set of tyres, which will play massively into teams' strategies.

Tensions between Ferrari teammates Hamilton and Charles Leclerc continue to heat up after boss Fred Vasseur labelled them "unmanageable."

Don't count out new world champion Kimi Antonelli who is always one to watch after an impressive season.

stories.headline: Heeney headlines returning Swans at pre-season training
stories.summary: After months of off-field turmoil in the fallout from the Pullman Hotel scandal, the Sydney Swans have welcomed back four AFL players for pre-season training.
stories.body:
The Sydney Swans have welcomed back their embattled AFL quartet to training after months of off-field turmoil following the Pullman Hotel scandal.

Isaac Heeney, Chad Warner, James Jordon and Riley Bice signalled their intent to resurrect their playing careers by taking part in the club's first-to-fourth-year pre-season training on Monday.

High-profile forward Tom Papley was also in attendance at Sydney's Bat and Ball Oval after being slapped with a three-game ban by the AFL for a positive roadside drug test.

Monday's session marked the first time Heeney, Warner, Bice and Jordon have officially trained with the Swans since serving a season-ending suspension for what the club termed a "serious breach of expected club behaviour and standards".

That AFL-endorsed suspension was also served by now-North Melbourne player Nick Blakey.

Separate from the bans, Heeney, Warner, Jordon and Blakey were under investigation after three women made reports of sexual assault to Victoria Police.

Police have since confirmed the players would not be charged due to insufficient evidence.

Civil claims are still being prepared against relevant parties.

Monday's session was a relaxed affair, with the club also welcoming draftees Caylen Murray, Mason McGroder, Mitchell Knevitt and Brady Wright.

Players undertook the usual pre-season conditioning programs, doing running drills before moving on to contest work and a short match simulation.

It wasn't the first time Heeney, Warner, Jordon and Rice had trained with teammates, having done informal sessions at Centennial Park.

Papley, one of the team's most experienced players, returned to training as he prepares to face Waverley Local Court for driving with a suspended licence on November 26.

The 30-year-old was pulled over by NSW Police for a random roadside drug test on November 2, with checks revealing his licence was suspended due to non-payment of a parking fine.

The initial roadside test returned a positive reading, and a secondary sample of oral fluid was taken.

That secondary sample returned a positive roadside test for the presence of cocaine and MDMA.

On top of his AFL ban for conduct unbecoming, Papley was fined $722 by police and his licence will be suspended for three months.

Papley spent most of Monday's training session with the rehabilitation group alongside fellow forwards Logan McDonald and Hayden McLean after undergoing surgery on both knees.

He suffered a grade-two medial collateral ligament strain in his right knee in the club's preliminary final loss to Fremantle, before undergoing an arthroscopy on his left knee to address a historic issue.

Papley will miss all pre-season matches and the club's opening rounds against Geelong, Essendon and GWS.
